unresolved: This is a methodology/critique paper, not a single-benchmark evaluation: n_models=9 and n_datasets=5 are sums across four unrelated case studies (4.1 mobile malware/AndroZoo+DREBIN with 2 SVM variants; 4.2 vulnerability discovery/Li et al. dataset with VulDeePecker+SVM+AutoSklearn; 4.3 authorship attribution/GCJ2017 with Abuhamad et al. and Caliskan et al. methods; 4.4 intrusion detection/Mirai dataset with KITSUNE+boxplot), so the counts do not represent one coherent evaluation grid.

No repetition/seed count is stated for any of the four case-study experiments; Table 1's caption reports 'standard deviation of the results ranges between 0-3%' without specifying how many runs/seeds produced that spread, so n_seeds is left null rather than assumed.

control_arm='clean' is an approximate mapping: this paper has no poisoning/backdoor setting. The closest analog is the 'correctly-labelled dataset' used as the clean reference point in Appendix A's label-noise cleansing experiment (Table 6, compared against a noisy and a cleansed variant).

n_baselines=3 counts only explicit baseline-vs-proposed-method comparisons introduced by the authors (SVM n-gram and AutoSklearn vs VulDeePecker in Section 4.2; boxplot method vs KITSUNE in Section 4.4). The Section 4.1 DREBIN/OPSEQS SVMs and Section 4.3 attribution methods are the primary objects of study rather than baselines, so they are excluded from this count.

The prevalence analysis (Section 3, 30 papers reviewed with inter-rater alpha=0.832) and the 49-author survey are the paper's other major empirical components but are not model/dataset evaluations, so they are not reflected in n_models/n_datasets.
